title: Agriculture
description: Agriculture is the practice of cultivating soil, growing crops, raising livestock, and harvesting biological products for food, fiber, and fuel

title: Archaeology
description: Archaeology is the scientific study of human activity, history, and prehistory through the recovery, documentation, and analysis of material culture and physical remains.

title: Egypt
description: Ancient Egyptian civilization was a major culture in northeastern Africa that lasted for over 3,000 years, centered around the fertile valley of the Nile River.

title: Algebra
description: Algebra is a major branch of mathematics that uses symbols and letters (called variables, such as x, y, or z) to represent unknown numbers and quantities.

title: Medicine
description: is the academic and practical training required to become a licensed physician or medical researcher, combining biomedical sciences with direct patient care.

title: Rome
description: Roman civilization was a classical society that grew from a small agricultural settlement along Italy's Tiber River into a vast Mediterranean empire.

title: Indigenous People
description: distinct social and cultural groups with ancestral ties to the lands they occupy or have been displaced from, characterized by self-identification, unique languages and traditions, and a special relationship with their natural environment.
